numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Returns True/False inconsistently when one of the intervals is empty (constructed with left==right and closed not equal to 'both' or 'neither' per the issue description). Example given: overlaps with an empty interval depends on which side of the point is closed, even though an empty interval contains no points and should never overlap.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Empty intervals contain no points at all, so they never overlap; overlaps should report False for overlaps with an empty interval.
trigger_conditions: Calling overlaps on Interval objects where an interval is empty (left == right) such as Interval(0, 0, closed="left") or Interval(0, 0, closed="right").
Specifically, overlaps results depend on which side is marked closed for these empty intervals (the bug described as mishandling empty intervals).
oracle_clues: The PR/issue text states that an empty interval such as Interval(0, 0, closed="left") contains no points, so it cannot share one with any interval; therefore empty intervals never overlap.
The whatsnew entry states: 'reporting an overlap with an empty interval such as Interval(0, 0, closed="left"), which contains no points; empty intervals now never overlap'.

category_specific_evidence: Mathematical property/formula violated: overlaps() incorrectly treats empty intervals as overlapping depending on which side of the point was closed, even though an empty interval contains no points and therefore cannot share a common point with any interval.

Test/expected concrete values: for test_overlaps_empty, expected overlap results are False for all three container intervals when the other interval is empty, i.e. expected = np.array([False, False, False]) and result = interval_container.overlaps(empty).
Empty interval definition used in reproduction: empty = pd.Interval(start + shift, start + shift, empty_closed) with empty_closed in {"left","right","neither"}.

Non-empty interval/container tuples used in reproduction: tuples = [(start, start + 3 * shift), (start + shift, start + shift), (start + 4 * shift, start + 5 * shift)] and interval_container = constructor.from_tuples(tuples, closed).

Explicit overlaps behavior from PR#67945 reproduction: pd.Interval(0, 1, "both").overlaps(pd.Interval(0, 0, "right")) == True; pd.Interval(0, 1, "both").overlaps(pd.Interval(0, 0, "left")) == False; pd.Interval(-1, 1, "both").overlaps(pd.Interval(0, 0, "neither")) == True.

Specification text added in code/docs: “empty intervals contain no points at all, so they never overlap” and “empty interval such as Interval(0, 0, closed="left") contains no points, so it cannot share one with any interval.”
reproduction_risks: Reproduction may depend on the exact interval closure semantics (closed="left"/"right"/"neither"/"both") and whether the reproduction uses the same empty interval construction pattern (start==end with specific closed side).
Reproduction results may vary by whether the method is called on Interval vs IntervalArray/IntervalIndex (the bug is stated for all three).
Some tests use parameterized constructor.from_tuples with start/shift and a separate container closed value; using different constructor/closed settings could change observed overlap outputs.
